mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating sum of visitors and dividing by 30 for both exhibits
Correct mean values for Exhibit A and Exhibit B

subparts.solution: Exhibit A: $\text{mean} = \frac{42 + 49 + 55 + 48 + \dots + 32}{30} = \frac{1644}{30} = 54.8\text{ visitors}$. Exhibit B: $\text{mean} = \frac{59 + 51 + 60 + 44 + \dots + 46}{30} = \frac{1711}{30} \approx 57.0\text{ visitors}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The mean of a dataset is the sum of values divided by sample size $n$.
step_by_step: For Exhibit A, sum all 30 values to get 1644, then divide by 30 to get 54.8.
For Exhibit B, sum all 30 values to get 1711, then divide by 30 to get approximately 57.0.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Transcribing numbers incorrectly when summing 30 values.
